name: NYC Department of Environmental Protection (NYC Water Board)
notes: Researched from public nyc.gov/dep pages only (no sign-in). My DEP Account sign-up needs the account number and the activation token printed on the bill; since the 2024 system change customers sign in with their registered email, and password resets send a verification code to the email on file; no sign-in MFA is described, so none is modelled. QuickPay makes a one-time payment without an account. Card payments carry a 2.25% convenience fee; bank (eCheck) payments are free. Autopay can use a bank account or a card and pays on the due date or a chosen day each month (a $50 one-time credit applies with monthly billing + e-billing; not modelled). Payment agreements need at least a 25% down payment and are set up with the Collections Unit (718-595-7890) by phone, email or at a Borough Office, so they are marked not offered online. Water and sewer charges belong to the property owner; there is no online stop-service request (ownership changes go through Customer Service), so cancel_service is marked not offered online. Most customers are billed quarterly.

sources.title: New Changes to Your My DEP Account

payment_arrangement.note: Payment agreements are not offered online. Call the DEP Collections Unit at 718-595-7890 or visit a Borough Office; at least a 25% down payment is required.

cancel_service.note: Stopping service is not offered online: water and sewer charges stay with the property owner. For a sale or ownership change call Customer Service at 718-595-7000.

help.title: How to pay your water and sewer bill
paragraphs: My DEP Account is free: pay, see bills and billing history, and get bills electronically. QuickPay makes a one-time online payment without an account; it posts the next business day.
Credit and debit card payments (Visa, MasterCard, Discover, American Express) carry a 2.25% convenience fee. Paying from a checking or savings account is free.
By phone, call 866-622-8292 at any hour for the automated payment line.
By mail, send a check or money order with your bill stub to NYC Water Board, P.O. Box 11863, Newark, NJ 07101-8163. Allow at least three business days for payments to post.
In person, pay by check or money order at a DEP Borough Office, or with cash at a Department of Finance Business Center.

help.title: Autopay
paragraphs: Autopay pays your bill from a bank account or credit card on the due date or on a day you choose each month. Only property owners can enroll, and you need a My DEP Account first.

Customers who sign up for Autopay and are enrolled in monthly billing and e-billing can receive a one-time $50 credit after their first automatic payment brings the balance to zero, as long as they stay enrolled and current for six months.
steps: Log in to My DEP Account.
Choose your payment method and monthly payment date.

help.title: Overdue charges and payment agreements
paragraphs: If you cannot pay in full, you can enter a payment agreement with at least a 25% down payment. Only the owner, or someone with power of attorney or a notarized letter of authorization, can sign one.

Payment agreements are set up with the Collections Unit at 718-595-7890 (weekdays 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.), by email, or at a Borough Office. Owners with a young child, a person 62 or older, a disabled person or a serious medical condition in the home may qualify for a lower down payment.
Seriously overdue charges can lead to a water shut-off, legal referral or inclusion in the property tax lien sale.

help.title: Sign up for My DEP Account
paragraphs: Choose Sign-up on the My DEP login page. You need your account number and the activation token printed on your bill; keep the token private because it unlocks your account.

Since the account system changed, you sign in with your registered email address. If you forget your password, request a verification code; it is sent only to the email on file and can take a few minutes to arrive.
steps: Enter your account number and activation token.
Enter your email address and create a password.
Verify your email with the code you receive.

help.title: How often you are billed
paragraphs: Most customers receive a bill about every three months based on metered water use. Some larger residential buildings pay a flat annual charge per unit, and a monthly billing option is available through My DEP Account.
Switching from paper bills to eBilling in My DEP Account is free.
